newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM Gujral sure coalition crisis will end.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM Gujral sure coalition crisis will end.

text.p: Indian Prime Minster Inder Kumar Gujral said on Tuesday that he was sure of an end to a current crisis in his United Front coalition resulting from the planned withdrawal of a regional party from the government.

"I do not see any possibility or any probability or any chance of a strain on the government. I would like to assure the nation that things are going smoothly," he told Asian News International in a videotaped interview.
"I am sure that wisdom has prevailed already that we must accomodate each others' point of view," he said.

He added that he had already spoken to two leaders of the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) after the southern based party issued a statement on Monday saying it planned to withdraw its four minister's from government, but would continue to support the coalition.
The DMK had said on Monday that the coalition had compromised on its dignity by allowing some of its partners to force their own agenda in the coalition.

It did not explain the differences, which party leaders said were targetted at the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), which had insisted on the removal from the coalition of a breakaway group of Gujral's Janata Dal party.
I am sure we would be able to sort it out in the next meeting of the steering committee (of the United Front)," Gujral said. "I am absolutely certain we will be able to bridge the difficulties."

The DMK accounts for less than 20 of the United Front's 178 lawmakers in India's 545-seat lower house of federal parliament. The coalition's survival depends on vital support from the Congress party's 140 members.
